Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  Fed on hold / tariff fog
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB patient / retaliation risk
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  targeted easing / weak demand
🇯🇵 Japan  Bullish  dovish tilt / weak yen
🇦🇺 Australia  Bearish  hawkish RBA / squeezed consumer
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing cycle / strong growth
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance beats the quarter — and pricing power is paid
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Housing-linked equities: a turnover recovery the market doubts
Copper miners: the AI-capex metal reprices
Bitcoin on course for its worst month since 2022
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
Nvidia tonight: guidance must beat AI-spending skepticism
Iran: the last-chance round of talks
$CEG  nuclear power meets the State of the Union  ↑
$WDAY  weak guide confirms the seat-based squeeze  ↓
body: Wednesday, February 25 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The AI scare eased but the policy fog did not: Wall Street bounced back on renewed tech vigor and easing AI concerns, and February consumer confidence improved even as a cloud over the labor market remains. Goolsbee called for a hold on cuts because inflation is ‘not good enough’. On trade, the new US tariff started at 10% while the administration works to lift it to 15%. We upgrade to Mixed: the VIX is back below 20, the Nvidia guide is pending.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.43% and the 10Y at 4.04%, a +61 bps 10Y−2Y spread that is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24). Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 13 bps and the 10Y 18 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24). Bloomberg notes the Treasury rally has stalled with the 10Y approaching 4%. The S&P 500 rose 0.77% to 6,890.07 and the VIX fell 6.95% to 19.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

New / Most Important: Two event risks land within hours: Trump is set to announce data-centre energy deals during his State of the Union address, and Nvidia reports after the bell. The tariff path is the third variable — a 10% rate that may rise to 15% keeps importers guessing. Fed Governor Cook warned AI could lift unemployment in the short term, a risk that would eventually argue for cuts.

Playbook ✓: Re-add equity beta in steps now that the VIX has closed below 20, through cyclicals with raised guidance and AI-infrastructure suppliers, not software or importers. Keep the IEF/TLT core while the 10Y holds below 4.22%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24). Cut back if the tariff moves to 15% without exemptions or if the VIX closes back above 20 from 19.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Macro Stance: Europe’s cycle is still improving relative to the US, but trade risk has moved from Washington’s court into Brussels’. The STOXX 600 is up 2.61% over 20 sessions versus a 0.87% fall for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Activity & Inflation: February business activity beat expectations as manufacturing bounced back, the cleanest cyclical signal in the region for months. EUR/USD slipped 0.35% to 1.1794 and is down 0.7% over 20 sessions, which eases financial conditions for exporters (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

New / Most Important: A top EU trade lawmaker told CNBC the US has breached the trade deal and Europe is ready to retaliate. Reuters’ strategist poll sees Europe’s strong start to the year likely to peter out, and Chancellor Merz heads to China seeking openings as global pressure builds.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Europe through the STOXX 600 and euro-area energy, but fund a DAX put spread as a hedge against EU retaliation; the DAX was flat in the prior session at 24,986.25 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Downgrade to neutral if Brussels formally triggers countermeasures or the next PMI round misses.

Macro Stance: China’s post-holiday restart mixes incremental easing with a firm trade stance. Shanghai eased homebuying rules in the latest property relief, while Beijing said it will decide on US tariff countermeasures in due course. That combination — small domestic steps, external optionality — argues for Mixed: better sentiment, unchanged demand. The asymmetric risk is that Beijing answers the new US tariff regime with countermeasures just as foreign investors return.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI, for January, dropped to 49.3, a contraction reading and the latest available official print. The February PMI is the test of whether the holiday-period consumption surge fed through to factories; until the index moves back above 50, treat activity as soft. Strong holiday travel and spending have to translate into hiring and wages before they change the consumption trend.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists, and benchmark lending rates were left unchanged for a ninth straight month. Credit demand, not credit supply, is the binding constraint, which is why Beijing keeps reaching for sector-specific measures rather than broad rate cuts.

Property: January new-home prices extended their decline as weak demand hounds the sector. Shanghai’s easing of homebuying rules is the first meaningful tier-one response, but one city cannot set a national floor. Confirmation would be slower price declines in the next monthly data and a pick-up in Shanghai transactions; absent that, developers stay an underweight.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing is keeping its powder dry on the new US tariff structure — countermeasures will be decided ‘in due course’ — while the unchanged LPR leaves fiscal and housing policy to do the lifting. The trade relationship with Japan is hardening: China imposed export controls on Japanese entities to curb what it calls ‘remilitarisation’.

Markets & Flows: Mainland trading reopened: the Shanghai Composite rose 0.87% to 4,117.41, while the Hang Seng fell 1.82% to 26,590.32 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). ASHR gained 0.38% to 34.14 and KWEB slipped 0.09% to 32.25, down 9.97% over 20 sessions; FXI fell 0.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). USD/CNY held at 6.9080, down 0.66% over 20 sessions — a firmer yuan (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

New / Most Important: Foreign money is coming back: SCMP reports US investors increasing their buying of Hong Kong and mainland stocks. The A-share reopening was orderly rather than euphoric, and Hong Kong gave back part of its prior jump, which tells us the flow is selective — into mainland beta and exporters, not into the internet platforms.

Playbook ✓: Own ASHR over KWEB and add Shanghai-exposed property names only on evidence that the rule changes lift transactions. Add to China beta if February loans beat forecasts; cut if Beijing announces tariff countermeasures that invite a US response. ⚠ Divergence: equity inflows and housing relief arrive while the official PMI sits at 49.3 and loan demand disappoints — sentiment is ahead of the data.

Macro Stance: Policy has tilted dovish: in a surprise move the government tapped two reflationists for the BOJ board, and PM Takaichi reportedly voiced concerns to the BOJ about further rate hikes. A slower hiking path plus a weak yen is the classic setup for Japanese exporters.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY rose 0.19% to 154.6350 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). The Nikkei 225 gained 0.87% to 57,321.09 and is up 6.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24); a Reuters poll sees the index breaching 60,000 by mid-2027 on earnings growth and foreign inflows.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities, now with a lower yen hedge given the dovish board picks. Risks: China’s export controls on Japanese entities escalate into supply-chain friction, or Washington and Tokyo step in against yen weakness. Re-hedge on any intervention headline.

Macro Stance: The labour market is tight enough to keep the RBA hawkish — unemployment held at 4.1%, leading to talk of another rate rise — and high wage growth reinforces the inflation challenge. Tightening into a weak household sector is negative for domestic earnings.

Demand & Financing: Economic confidence sits at a 13-year low. AUD/USD fell 0.71% to 0.7061 but is still up 2.11% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 was flat at 9,022.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Playbook ✓: Keep a long AUD/USD core — UniSuper calls the currency undervalued and is increasing its hedging — but stay underweight domestic consumer and property-linked names. Prefer copper-linked miners. Reverse if the RBA signals it is done tightening or AUD/USD loses its 20-session gain.

Monetary & Activity: NBP Governor Glapiński says inflation will be close to target within two years (xyz.pl: ‘w ciągu dwóch lat inflacja będzie bliska celu’), keeping the easing path open. The 2025 central-budget deficit came in smaller than the budget allowed (‘Deficyt mniejszy niż dopuszczał budżet’). The new soft spot is housing: Poland recorded its first annual housing-price fall since 2013.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN rose 0.28% to 3.5748 and EUR/PLN held at 4.2189; EPOL slipped 0.39% to 37.95 and the WIG20TR ETF fell 0.61% to 68.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Banks led the decline — PEO.WA fell 1.71% and PKO.WA 1.42% — while KGH.WA rose 1.96% and is up 12.83% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Money.pl called it a ‘red Tuesday’ on the GPW with banks dragging the index down.

Companies: KGHM has a new CEO after the supervisory board’s decision (Money.pl: ‘KGHM ma nowego prezesa. Jest decyzja’), ending the leadership uncertainty at the copper producer. PKN.WA is up 9.02% and PGE.WA 9.43% over 20 sessions, while CDR.WA is down 9.71% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Security & New Development: Warsaw has banned Chinese cars from military bases and barred personnel from connecting phones to them, part of tighter security screening of Chinese technology. For investors the signal is that security policy, not price, increasingly decides procurement — a tailwind for domestic and NATO-aligned suppliers and a risk for Chinese brands selling into the Polish market.

Playbook ✓: Use bank weakness to add PEO.WA and PKO.WA into a likely cut, and hold KGH.WA for the copper upswing under new management. Hedge housing exposure: the first annual price fall since 2013 argues against developers. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP sounds relaxed about inflation, yet the zloty slipped and banks sold off on the day — the market is questioning how much easing the banks can absorb.

Narrative: The AI-disruption trade paused rather than reversed: software stocks rebounded as Anthropic announced new partnerships, and XLK rose 1.3% in the prior session but is still down 3.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: Workday sank on weak revenue guidance — the market is still punishing seat-based software on forward numbers, not on the reported quarter. MSFT rose 1.18% but remains down 17.28% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

EPS Upside Watch: Hardware franchises carry the upside: AAPL rose 2.24% to 272.14 and is up 6.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). The cost side is the risk — memory-price inflation is now hitting PC makers’ guidance.

⚡ Breaking Convention: One relief day does not make a bottom: ORCL rose 3.42% yet is down 19.9% over 20 sessions, and PLTR fell 1.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Rent the bounce in software, do not own it; the next guidance season will show whether seat counts are falling.

Narrative: Communication services is trading on AI capex and new revenue lines rather than on ads: XLC rose 0.69% but is down 1.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Meta is testing stablecoin payments as digital currencies take off.

Reported: No major platform reported in the window; the news was supply contracts. Barron’s reports the AMD–Meta deal moved Nvidia and kept Wall Street bullish ahead of earnings, underscoring Meta’s role as one of the largest AI buyers.

EPS Upside Watch: Netflix is the rebound candidate: NFLX rose 2.66% but is still down 8.94% over 20 sessions, and DIS rose 1.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). META at 639.30 is down 4.92% over 20 sessions, so capex worries are priced (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Payments, not ads, may be Meta’s next re-rating lever: a stablecoin rail would monetise its user base without more data-centre spend. That is the opposite of the capex-fatigue narrative.

Narrative: Financials remain hostage to private credit: UBS now sees private-credit defaults reaching 15% in a worst case. XLF rose 0.49% but is down 4.55% over 20 sessions, with BAC down 1.29% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: Outside the US the prints were solid: HSBC lifted its earnings target as annual profit dipped but beat estimates. In the US, GS rose 1.12% while JPM slipped 0.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

EPS Upside Watch: Wealth and markets businesses are carrying bank earnings — HSBC’s beat came with a higher target — which favours diversified franchises over lenders with heavy private-credit or software-loan exposure. In the US, trading-heavy franchises benefit from the elevated volatility of the past month.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A worst-case default scenario of 15% would be a fund-level problem first; banks that lend senior to these funds may gain pricing power. Stay underweight XLF, but keep a watch-list of senior lenders to buy if contagion stays contained.

Narrative: Oil hit seven-month highs as tensions rose before US–Iran talks, then eased: Brent fell 1.01% to 70.77 but is up 7.9% over 20 sessions, and XLE is up 11.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: EOG beat profit estimates on strong output and higher gas prices — US shale is delivering volume and price at once.

EPS Upside Watch: CVX is up 10.65% and XOM 10.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24); with Brent above its 20-session reference of 65.59, Q1 upstream estimates still look too low.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gas is the contrarian leg: Henry Hub is down 57.13% over 20 sessions at 2.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24), yet EOG cited higher gas prices in its beat — realised prices lag the futures, so gas-weighted producers face a weaker Q2.

Narrative: Industrials own the bottleneck of the AI build: data centres are being hit by power delays and equipment shortages. XLI rose 1.23% and is up 7.67% over 20 sessions; GE is up 17.14% and CAT 20.81% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: The window’s industrial prints were mixed outside the AI chain: Kratos fell after the drone maker’s earnings beat, a reminder that defence names need guidance upgrades, not beats. The bar for the AI-power suppliers is the same: order intake and pricing, not the quarter.
EPS Upside Watch: Equipment shortages mean pricing power for transformer, switchgear and turbine makers; Trump’s planned data-centre energy deals would add orders.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Aerospace is catching up: BA rose 1.28% but is still down 6.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Own grid equipment over airframes until deliveries improve.

Narrative: The consumer data improved at the margin: February confidence rose though the labor-market cloud remains. XLY rose 1.52% but is down 4.56% over 20 sessions, with AMZN down 12.52% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: Home Depot topped estimates for the first time in a year even as demand for projects remains muted; HD rose 1.99% to 384.48 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Cava jumped 26% on surprise same-store sales growth driven by menu prices.

EPS Upside Watch: Pricing power is the theme: Cava’s same-store growth came from menu prices, which shows that brands with loyal traffic can still pass on costs. Upside sits with restaurants and specialty retailers that can price, not with discretionary importers facing a tariff that may rise to 15%.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bearish housing-turnover case did not show up in Home Depot’s numbers: mortgage rates below 6% may be doing more than the January sales data suggested. TSLA rose 2.39% but is down 5.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Narrative: Staples have become the expensive hiding place: the Motley Fool notes they have not been this expensive in 25 years. XLP rose 0.87% and is up 8.41% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: No large staples name reported in the window; WMT rose 0.75% to 126.75 and COST 1.26% to 998.43 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

EPS Upside Watch: With valuations stretched, even in-line prints will struggle to lift multiples; the upside is limited to names with volume recovery rather than price-led growth. Big-box retailers, the largest weights in the ETF, offer little room for positive surprise at these multiples.

⚡ Breaking Convention: As the VIX falls back below 20 (19.55) the defensive premium is the first thing to deflate (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Rotate out of XLP into cyclicals with raised guidance.

Narrative: Healthcare is split between pharma resilience and managed-care stress: XLV slipped 0.42%, UNH fell 2.97% and is down 22.09% over 20 sessions, and LLY fell 1.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: Fresenius Medical Care dropped after its outlook underwhelmed — care providers are being sold on guidance just like software.

EPS Upside Watch: Capital markets are open for medtech: Medtronic’s diabetes unit MiniMed eyes a $7.9 billion valuation in a US IPO, which should crystallise value for the parent. Separations and listings are the sector’s cleanest catalysts while policy risk keeps the insurers out of favour.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Managed care is the sector’s value trap, not its value opportunity: UNH at 273.95 keeps falling despite the defensive bid (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Own pharma and medtech separations, avoid insurers.

Narrative: Copper jumped as China traders cheered the prospect of lower US levies: front-month copper rose 2.6% to 5.92 and FCX 3.55%, up 11.11% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). XLB is up 6.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: Gold slipped from a three-week high on dollar strength and profit-taking; gold fell 0.94% to 5,176.30 while NEM was flat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper miners have the cleanest upside: the metal is down just 1.02% over 20 sessions while FCX is up 10.97%, and lower US levies would support Chinese demand (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver keeps outperforming gold in the short term — SI=F rose 1.08% and is up 19.07% over five sessions, while gold fell (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). The metals bid is broadening, not just hedging.

Narrative: Real estate is an AI-immune income trade with a rate tailwind: mortgage rates dropped below 6%, matching the lowest since 2022. XLRE rose 0.28% and is up 6.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: GO Residential REIT announced accretive acquisitions and raised guidance — residential landlords are using cheaper capital to grow. Accretive deals at today’s funding costs are the clearest sign that the sector’s earnings trough is behind it.

EPS Upside Watch: Falling funding costs — the 10Y is down 18 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24) — should lift 2026 guidance at levered REITs, as GO Residential’s raise shows.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Home Depot’s beat suggests housing activity is steadier than January sales implied; the risk to REITs is a stalled Treasury rally, not weak demand.

Narrative: Utilities have the AI power story and now the earnings to match: Constellation topped estimates and CEG jumped 6.41% to 312.64 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). XLU is up 10.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: Dominion detailed a $65B, 5-year spending plan, extending the rate-base growth that drives regulated EPS.

EPS Upside Watch: Trump’s planned data-centre energy deals in the State of the Union are a direct catalyst for nuclear and gas generators; NEE is up 11.95% and VST 8.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Merchant generators with uncontracted capacity have the most torque to new long-term supply deals.
⚡ Breaking Convention: The sector is priced as growth now: a stalled bond rally — the 10Y approaching 4% — is the main threat to multiples, not demand.

Narrative: European autos bounced but the structural picture worsened: German car exports to China plunged by a third in 2025. The SXAP tracker rose 1.95% to 46.29 and is up 2.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
Reported: Stellantis dealers in Europe joined the push for EU relief as sales lag; STLA rose 2.24% but is down 19.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

EPS Upside Watch: The relative winners are names with cost programmes: MBG.DE is up 3.51% and RNO.PA 2.97% over 20 sessions, while VOW3.DE is down 0.68% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Upside surprises will come from cost cuts, not volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention: A retaliatory EU–US cycle would hit carmakers on both sides of the Atlantic; sell the bounce in SXAP rather than chase it.
Narrative: Semis led the rebound: SOXX rose 1.46% and is up 5.53% over 20 sessions, TSM jumped 4.25% to 385.75 (up 15.94% over 20) and AMD 8.77% to 213.84 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

Reported: HP warned the memory-chip crunch will linger next year and flagged a PC sales slump — bad for PC makers, good for memory pricing. MU slipped 0.7% to 418.01 but is up 7.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
EPS Upside Watch: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25, and the AMD–Meta deal kept Wall Street bullish into the print. INTC jumped 5.71% and is up 8.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

⚡ Breaking Convention: AMD’s 8.77% jump on its Meta win cuts against the single-supplier narrative (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Hyperscalers are diversifying their silicon, which spreads AI capex across more chip designers and favours the foundry and equipment owners — TSM and ASML — that get paid whichever design wins. Own the toll roads, not the individual designers.

Rewarded: Pricing power and capex leverage: Cava jumped 26% on same-store sales growth driven by menu prices, Constellation topped estimates and CEG rose 6.41% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24), and Home Depot beat for the first time in a year.

Punished: Weak guidance and growth disappointments: Workday sank on weak revenue guidance, Lucid widely missed and forecast slowing EV growth, Kratos fell even after a beat and Fresenius Medical Care dropped on an underwhelming outlook.

Pattern: The reaction function is unchanged: forward guidance first, AI exposure second, the reported quarter third. Beats without guidance support (Kratos) are sold; companies that can raise prices or ride AI-power demand are paid. The tape also rewards visibility — utilities with multi-year capex plans and restaurants with proven traffic trade at a premium to companies whose demand depends on discretionary software or EV budgets.
Attention into EPS: Nvidia’s report on Feb. 25 collides with Wall Street skepticism over AI spending; the bar is guidance on hyperscaler demand and margins.

Playbook: Buy post-earnings strength only where guidance rose or pricing power is explicit; fade beats with flat outlooks. Into Nvidia, use call spreads; after the print, follow guidance, not the headline beat.

Attention Gap: Investors fixated on January’s weak home sales, yet Home Depot beat for the first time in a year and mortgage rates are below 6%. The 10Y is down 18 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24), a tailwind the housing complex has barely priced.

Exposure & Risk: Express via HD (384.48, down 0.53% over 20 sessions) and XLRE (up 6.09%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Risk: the Treasury rally stalls near 4% and pushes mortgage rates back up.

Attention Gap: Copper jumped on the prospect of lower US levies, and data-centre equipment shortages point to demand that outruns supply. Front-month copper is still down 1.02% over 20 sessions at 5.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24), so the metal has not priced the AI build. The equities have started to move while the commodity lags — that gap is the opportunity.

Exposure & Risk: Own FCX (up 10.97% over 20 sessions) and KGH.WA (up 12.83% over five sessions, new CEO) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Risk: a weak Nvidia guide that hits AI-capex expectations, or renewed US–China tariff escalation.

Market Context: BTC closed at 64,080.04 at the prior completed daily close, down 0.83% and 12.24% over 20 sessions; ETH slipped 0.14% to 1,852.97 and SOL rose 1.65% to 79.04 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). IBIT is down 26.42% and MSTR 22.4% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin is heading for its worst month since the crypto collapse of June 2022, and US demand has been negative for a record 40 days as ‘bitcoin zero’ searches peak. Coinbase is broadening beyond crypto into equities and ETFs — a hedge against a long winter. Big platforms are still building payment rails: Meta is testing stablecoin payments, which keeps the infrastructure story alive even as token prices fall.

Playbook: Stay underweight tokens until US demand turns positive and BTC reclaims its 20-session reference of 73,019.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Prefer COIN over MSTR: diversification into equities cushions it if crypto volumes stay weak.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY rose 0.18% to 97.88 but Citigroup’s hedge-fund clients sold the dollar around the Supreme Court tariff ruling, and Asian currencies hit a 16-month high as the yuan gained. TLT rose 0.18% to 89.90 and IEF is up 1.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24); the 10Y at 4.04% sits inside a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24).

Credit Check: HYG slipped 0.07% to 80.81 and is down 0.46% over 20 sessions while LQD is up 0.68% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Listed spreads are calm; the stress is in private vehicles, where UBS sees worst-case defaults of 15%.

Portfolio Implication: Keep IG over HY, stay underweight USD against Asian currencies, and hold duration while the 10Y stays below 4.22% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-24). Use equity strength into Nvidia to rebalance toward non-US and real assets.

What Is Priced: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25 into Wall Street skepticism over AI spending. NVDA closed at 192.85, up 4.26% over five sessions and 3.42% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24) — the stock has priced a beat, not a step-up in guidance.

Conditional Expression: If guidance rises, buy SOXX and the foundry chain (TSM, ASML) and fund it from staples and software. If guidance only meets, rotate within AI toward power and grid suppliers (XLU, XLI), whose revisions do not depend on one print.
Risk: A hyperscaler-diversification story — the AMD–Meta deal — could cap Nvidia’s multiple even on a good print, while a miss would revive the AI-disruption sell-off.

What Is Priced: A last-chance round of US–Iran talks is nearing as the US military buildup worries Iranians, and oil eased as Iran said it is prepared to take steps to reach a deal. Brent at 70.77 is up 4.97% over five sessions and gold at 5,176.30 up 5.51% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24) — a partial war premium.

Conditional Expression: If talks fail, own XLE and GLD and hedge airlines; Brent’s 20-session reference of 65.59 becomes the floor (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). If a deal lands, sell the oil premium and rotate to consumer discretionary and oil-importing Asia.
Risk: A supply shock would lift inflation just as Goolsbee says current inflation is ‘not good enough’ for cuts — a stagflation hit to both bonds and equities.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25. Thesis: AI demand is broadening rather than fading — the AMD–Meta deal kept the Street bullish on Nvidia ahead of earnings — and skepticism over AI spending sets a beatable bar for guidance.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 192.85, up 0.68% in the prior session and 3.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). The hurdle is guidance strong enough to break the stock’s range; risk is share loss to custom and AMD silicon. Cut on a close below the 20-session reference.

Catalyst & Thesis: Constellation topped earnings estimates, and Trump is set to announce data-centre energy deals during the State of the Union. Thesis: firm, carbon-free power is the scarcest input in the AI build, and policy is now pushing hyperscalers to buy it.

Price Hurdle & Risk: CEG closed at 312.64 after a 6.41% jump, up 9.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24). Risk: the speech disappoints on specifics, or the bond rally stalls and compresses utility multiples; trim if CEG gives back the earnings-day gain.

Catalyst & Thesis: Workday sank on weak revenue guidance, and Bloomberg reports investors are dumping software stocks with earnings unable to stop it. Thesis: AI agents compress seat-based HR and finance software growth, and the guide is the first hard evidence.

Price Hurdle & Risk: The hurdle for the short is a failed rebound after the post-earnings drop or a further guidance cut. Risk: Anthropic-style partnerships reframe incumbents as AI distributors and spark a short squeeze; cover on a reclaimed post-earnings gap.

Observed Attention: Yahoo Finance reports TSLA is down 11% in 2026 and Reddit is losing faith fast. TSLA rose 2.39% to 409.38 in the prior session but is down 5.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-24).
